title: schema-first-output-with-gradual-strictness-and-stream-recovery
author: Priya Mehta
description:
Motivation: Production apps require both high fidelity structured outputs and resilient streaming behavior when the model deviates from a schema. This PR introduces a schema-first output mode (typed contracts) with a graduated strictness model and a streaming recovery path that preserves partial results instead of hard aborts. Key ideas: 1) response_format supports 'typed_schema' with a 'strictness' param that ranges from lenient->strict; 2) streaming path adds a soft-fallback branch which emits a best-effort 'repair_hint' event and continues with a canonicalized payload; 3) when validation fails during a tool/function call, the runtime attempts a single automatic repair pass before invoking tool failure handlers; 4) OpenAI-compat layer maps these contract failures into structured error objects and 'function_call' adjustments per spec compatibility. Changes include API surface, runtime streaming changes, SDK mappings, console UX, and metrics.

What changed (high-level): implemented typed contract parsing and schema registry lookup; added heuristic_repair module that can fix common issues (missing keys, type coercion, truncated arrays); added stream_recovery path that queues last-good tokens and emits repair_hint + contract_violation events instead of closing stream; exposed response_format: {"type":"typed_schema","schema_id":"<id>","strictness":"lenient|balanced|strict"} in server API; SDK changes in openai_compat to translate old 'function_call' behaviors into tool_call + contract_failure semantics.

Checklist: - [x] API design doc in linear (ENG-4721) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] integration with console viewer - [x] metrics and alerts added - [x] docs draft in repo - [x] backwards compatibility gate guarded behind feature flag

Related: Linear ENG-4721, ENG-4803. Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4721/typed-contracts; spec: docs/api/response_format_v2.md

Commits: feat(schema): add typed_contracts registry and parser; feat(validation): heuristic_repair and strict toggle; fix(stream): preserve-token-queue on validation-fail; feat(sdk): openai_compat mapping for contract errors; docs: response_format v2 and examples; test: contract streaming integration tests.

Files touched (high level): API contract layer, runtime stream handler, validation heuristics, SDK compatibility layer, console schema viewer, tests, docs.

Review conversation summary: Reviewer Lucas asked for clearer failure codes and to avoid failing user streams for recoverable problems; author implemented contract violation events and improved error code taxonomy (CONTRACT_VIOLATION_RECOVERED, CONTRACT_VIOLATION_HARD). Samira requested additional unit tests around function/tool calling when the model returns JSON-like but with wrong types; added test harness and a flaky-model simulator. Evan pointed out potential perf regression on high QPS due to extra validation; we added a fast-path that bypasses heuristic repair for strict=true and added batching for validation to amortize cost. QA ran integration tests and reported one intermittent failure on low-memory nodes; fixed by moving small buffer to disk-backed queue in edge case. Final approvals from Lucas and Evan before merge.

CI summary: 12/12 checks passed in final run. Flaky lint failure earlier addressed in commit 5. Integration suite reported one transient failure in earlier run; rerun was green.

Runtime behavior/compat notes: Feature is behind feature flag 'typed_contracts_v1'; default strictness is 'lenient' for existing customers. OpenAI compatibility: SDK's openai_compat layer will translate contract events into older 'function_call' error shapes for older clients. New telemetry: schema.validation.result, schema.validation.repair.count, schema.validation.latency_ms, stream.recovery.count.

Release notes: - New 'typed_schema' response_format with lenient|balanced|strict modes; - Streaming now preserves partial outputs and emits repair_hint events rather than abruptly closing for recoverable schema violations; - Automatic one-shot heuristic repair for common JSON issues before tool invocation; - OpenAI-compat mapping preserves backwards behavior while exposing richer error taxonomy; - Feature behind flag and not enabled by default.
commits: add heuristic_repair module and strict mode toggle
stream: implement preservation queue and repair_hint events
sdk(openai_compat): map contract failures to function_call errors
tests: contract streaming integration and flaky-model simulator
infra: feature flag rollout for typed_contracts_v1
review_comments: Lucas Tran: Please avoid aborting streams for recoverable schema mismatches; prefer eventing so apps can surface partial results. -- addressed in stream_recovery.go and added repair_hint event.
Samira Patel: Add unit tests for tool/function calls failing due to type coercion; include a simulated model that returns string where array expected. -- added integration test and simulator harness.
Evan Brooks: Concerned about perf impact at high QPS; propose fast-path bypass when strict=true and batch validation. -- implemented validation batching and strict fast-path.
QA (Marina Chen): Found intermittent failure on low-memory CI node; moved small queue to disk-backed buffer to mitigate. -- fixed and added CI test.
release_notes_short: automatic heuristic repair before tool invocation

Watch metrics: schema.validation.repair.count and stream.recovery.count during rollout
